title: Airbus and Thales win order for SpainSat replacement
summary: Airbus Defence and Space and Thales Alenia Space have secured a contract to build a replacement military communications satellite for Spain. The deal is part of ongoing efforts to establish a space joint venture involving Airbus, Thales, and Leonardo.
company: Airbus Defence and Space, Thales Alenia Space

title: U.S. Air Force expands Blue Origin rocket cargo contract
summary: The U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory increased Blue Origin's contract by $11.7 million to study the use of space rockets for point-to-point deliveries.

title: Space Force awards K2 Space $22.9 million for laser communications demonstration
summary: The U.S. Space Force has awarded K2 Space a $22.9 million contract to demonstrate laser communications using two satellites equipped with optical terminals. The goal is to enhance connectivity between military systems in orbit.

title: China launches secretive TJS-27 pair, orbits next-gen Tianlian relay sat
summary: China launched a Long March 6A rocket carrying a secretive TJS-27 satellite pair and a next-generation Tianlian relay satellite into a new orbit. The mission enhances China's on-orbit communications relay capabilities.

title: Sending repurposed Mars rover to the moon could cost more than $1 billion
summary: Converting a Mars rover engineering model into a lunar rover could cost NASA over $1 billion, a claim disputed by the agency's administrator.

title: Spain commits up to $2.3 billion for national military communications for IRIS²
summary: Spain will allocate between €1.6 billion and €2 billion ($1.8 to $2.3 billion) to develop a national military satellite communications constellation as part of the IRIS² program. This investment aims to enhance Spain's secure military communications capabilities.

title: Inside the effort to show Congress what war in space looks like
summary: The Space Force Association’s National Spacepower Center is creating an unclassified environment to demonstrate satellite threats and their potential impacts on Earth for Congress. This effort aims to visualize the consequences of warfare in space.

title: Space Force picks 15 companies for $981 million training range contract
summary: The U.S. Space Force has selected 15 companies to compete for a $981 million contract to develop satellites, sensors, and systems for realistic military space training exercises.

title: NASA still assessing Starliner-1 flight opportunities
summary: NASA is making progress with Boeing's CST-100 Starliner but has not yet set a date for its next flight. The agency continues to assess flight opportunities for the Starliner-1 mission.

title: The new space wars: lessons from Ukraine and the Middle East
summary: The article discusses the evolving nature of space warfare, drawing lessons from conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East. It highlights the growing importance of space in modern military strategies.

title: The 1st 'three-headed' asteroid | Space photo of the day for Aug. 3, 2026
summary: New images reveal what astronomers believe is the first-known 'trilobate' or three-headed asteroid in our solar system. This discovery could provide insights into the formation and structure of asteroids.

title: On this day in space! NASA launches MESSENGER spacecraft to orbit Mercury
summary: NASA launched the MESSENGER spacecraft to orbit Mercury for the first time, aiming to search for clues of water on the planet.

title: 13 amazing things to see during the total solar eclipse on Aug. 12
summary: On August 12, 2026, a total solar eclipse will offer unique viewing opportunities, including the solar corona. Additional phenomena will also be visible during the event.

title: Astronomers watch a black hole's feeding frenzy end with a bad case of cosmic indigestion
summary: Astronomers observed a black hole's feeding frenzy conclude with a powerful windy outburst. This cosmic indigestion marks the end of its intense accretion phase.

title: Is the Nocs Provisions Lite View spotting scope a good alternative to a traditional telescope?
summary: The Nocs Provisions Lite View spotting scope is evaluated as an alternative to traditional telescopes, offering detailed views of the moon and bright star clusters in a compact design.

title: AI is ready to run spacecraft. Is the space industry ready for it? (op-ed)
summary: Artificial intelligence is poised to assist in managing increasingly complex satellite constellations, but the space industry's readiness for AI integration remains uncertain.

title: Gears of War: E-Day: Release date, platforms & everything else we know about Marcus Fenix's return
summary: The news discusses the release date and details of 'Gears of War: E-Day', a prequel to the Gears of War series. It highlights that the game is built from scratch and returns to the series' roots.

title: Double digits! Air-launched 'Talon A' hypersonic vehicle notches big flight milestone
summary: Stratolaunch has conducted over 10 flights with its Talon-A hypersonic vehicle, an autonomous, air-launched craft capable of reaching speeds five times the speed of sound.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 2, 1971: Apollo 15 makes 1st-ever televised liftoff from the moon
summary: On Aug. 2, 1971, NASA's Apollo 15 mission achieved the first-ever televised liftoff from the moon, marking a significant milestone for live TV broadcasting from space.

title: From Hardspace to Clearspace: How space salvage games compare to real debris removal
summary: The article compares space salvage games like 'Hardspace' to real-world space debris removal efforts, highlighting the challenges of cleaning up orbital debris. It emphasizes the growing importance of active debris removal missions in the space industry.

title: Ike Theriot Helps Prepare Astronauts to Work on the Moon
summary: Ike Theriot leads NASA's Flight Operations Surface Testing to prepare astronauts for lunar exploration. His career path to NASA involved military service and a focus on extravehicular activity operations.

title: NASA Brings Space Exploration to the FIFA World Cup
summary: NASA showcased space exploration at the FIFA World Cup's fan festival in Houston, attracting over 500,000 visitors. The exhibit highlighted missions like Artemis, the Moon Base, and the International Space Station.

title: APOD: 2026 August 3 – Vaporizing Meteor Photobombs the Lacerta Nebula
summary: A meteor vaporizing in the sky appears to 'photobomb' the Lacerta Nebula in an image featured as NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) for August 3, 2026. The APOD series highlights daily cosmic images with explanations by professional astronomers.

title: APOD: 2026 August 2 – A Fire Rainbow over West Virginia
summary: APOD features an image of a 'fire rainbow' over West Virginia, explained by professional astronomers. The phenomenon is caused by ice crystals in high-altitude clouds refracting sunlight.

title: APOD: 2026 August 1 – Buck Moon and Belt of Venus
summary: APOD features an image of the Buck Moon and Belt of Venus, a traditional name for the July full moon, with an explanation by a professional astronomer.

title: What’s Up: August 2026 Skywatching Tips from NASA
summary: NASA shares skywatching tips for August 2026, highlighting a solar eclipse, the Perseids meteor shower, Venus at its brightest, and a deep partial lunar eclipse. The month's celestial events are detailed in a skywatching transcript.

title: NASA to Host Florida Event Celebrating American Air, Space Leadership
summary: NASA will host a news conference at Kennedy Space Center in Florida on August 14 to preview a new event. The announcement will be held in the XLV Hangar at the Shuttle Landing Facility.

title: NASA’s Newest Wind Tunnel Opens at NASA Langley
summary: NASA opened its first major new wind tunnel in over 40 years, the Flight Dynamics Research Facility at NASA Langley, to support aeronautics, exploration, and science goals. The facility was inaugurated on July 31, 2026, with NASA leadership and Virginia officials in attendance.

title: TB 26-05 Webbings for Use in Elevated Oxygen Environments
summary: Flammability test results for commercial-off-the-shelf webbings meeting NASA standards for elevated oxygen environments were reported, with a 60% Kevlar®/40% PBI webbing from Sturges Manufacturing Company passing NASA-STD-6001B Test 1.

title: NASA, SpaceX Advance Wind Tunnel Tests for Starship Rocket
summary: NASA and SpaceX have completed wind tunnel tests on SpaceX's Super Heavy Version 3 rocket booster to prepare for the Artemis III mission. The tests, conducted at NASA's Ames Research Center, aimed to study aerodynamic forces during re-entry.

title: Boeing’s Starliner set for potential 2026 cargo run to ISS
summary: Boeing's CST-100 Starliner spacecraft is undergoing redesign work for a potential cargo mission to the International Space Station (ISS) by 2026. CEO Kelly Ortberg highlighted the ongoing modifications during a recent announcement.

title: Starbase Pad 1 Retrofits Progress as Block 3 Flights Start
summary: SpaceX has completed two flights from the newly designed Pad 2 at Starbase while retrofitting efforts continue on Pad 1. The shift to Block 3 flights marks a new phase in SpaceX's launch operations.

title: Blue Origin continues rebuilding LC-36, prepares testing alternatives for New Glenn second stage
summary: Blue Origin is continuing the reconstruction of Launch Complex 36 (LC-36) and exploring alternative testing methods for the second stage of its New Glenn rocket following a recent pad explosion during a static fire test.

title: Ship 40’s flawless flight promotes next mission catch potential
summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13 successfully completed its mission with Ship 40 returning intact, demonstrating its reliability for future missions. This flawless flight paves the way for potential in-flight catch attempts in upcoming missions.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9 and Chang Zheng rockets set to launch this week
summary: Five orbital launches are scheduled this week, including a Chang Zheng 6A rocket in China and a Falcon 9 rocket. The launches are part of ongoing global spaceflight activities.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: NASA's Juno mission reveals surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io after two flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the volcanic moon's geology.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to conduct hot-fire tests for the second stage of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket at the Stennis B-2 test stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the New Glenn rocket for future missions.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones for SpaceX during its third attempt. This marks another step forward in SpaceX's Starship development program.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 crew successfully docked with the International Space Station (ISS), increasing the station's crew size. A U.S. spacewalk also completed repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: Path to Starship Flight 13 requires additional Booster 20 test
summary: SpaceX is preparing for its 13th Starship flight, targeting a launch no earlier than July 23, but requires additional testing of Booster 20. The delay is due to the need for further validation before the next attempt.

title: TEC Business to Business website
summary: The TEC Business to Business website reported on an unspecified space industry news. No specific details about the content were provided.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of significant contributions by the European Space Agency.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time during a drone flight at ESA's ESTEC technical center in the Netherlands. The payload was carried by a drone, marking a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying by using a coronagraph to block the Sun's light, creating an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona. This technology will allow scientists to observe the Sun's outer atmosphere without the need for a physical eclipse.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and foster collaboration with Europe's space industry on September 16-17 in the Netherlands.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technologies for next-generation antennas, highlighting their role in steering and improving antenna performance. This innovation is crucial for enhancing communication systems in space applications.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber, confirming its electronics are fit for space. The mission is now cleared for launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: ESA is hosting events to present the follow-up to the Council Meeting at Ministerial Level 2025 (CM25), detailing planned activities and industrial opportunities across ESA programs.

title: True Anomaly Chases an Evading Target
summary: True Anomaly successfully executed the first in-space pursuit of an evading target as part of the VICTUS HAZE mission. This achievement marks a significant milestone in space operations and defense capabilities.

title: AFRL Adds $11.7M to Blue Origin’s Point-to-Point Cargo Contract
summary: AFRL increased Blue Origin's contract by $11.7M to study point-to-point cargo delivery using its launcher. The funding will explore the feasibility of using Blue Origin's technology for rapid global logistics.

title: K2 Space Raises $500M Series D at $6.8B Valuation
summary: K2 Space raised $500 million in a Series D funding round, valuing the company at $6.8 billion. This brings K2 Space's total financing to over $1 billion since 2022.

title: NordSpace Funds NVD Amid Canada’s Export Push
summary: NordSpace Ventures invested in North Vector Dynamics, a company developing sovereign missile capabilities. This move aligns with Canada's push to enhance its defense exports.

title: Report: Our Launch Cadence Forecast For Next-Gen Rockets
summary: The article discusses the expected flight cadence ramp for next-gen reusable rockets, including New Glenn, Neutron, Nova, Terran R, and Eclipse. It aims to forecast how frequently these rockets will be launched.

title: Payload Field Guide: European Launchers
summary: Europe is rapidly developing new launch capabilities, but progress is slower than desired. The continent aims to enhance its space industry competitiveness.

title: Hop Aero Wants to Deliver Cargo via Rocket
summary: Hop Aero, a new startup, launched on Y Combinator with its autonomous suborbital rocket named Rook. The company aims to deliver cargo via rocket.

title: Payload Pioneers: Where Are They Now?
summary: The Payload Pioneers program has recognized 90 young professionals in the space industry since 2023. The article updates on the progress of some of the 30-under-30 awardees.

title: Outlier Space Raises $7.3M to Build New Zealand’s First Reentry Vehicle
summary: Outlier Space secured $7.35M to develop New Zealand's first reentry vehicle for microgravity research and return missions, with a debut flight planned for 2028.

title: ESA taps Aalyria to build deep-space network hub
summary: ESA has selected Aalyria to construct a network-operations center for deep-space communication, enabling reliable data sharing among spacecraft across the solar system.

title: AccelerCom and Eclipse Space Reveals Details of D2D Collaboration
summary: AccelerComm has completed two engineering engagements with Eclipse Space to define the physical-layer architecture for its next-generation Direct-to-Device spacecraft. The collaboration focuses on advancing satellite infrastructure technology.

title: K2 Space Secures Series D Funding After Hitting $1 Billion Contract Value Milestone
summary: K2 Space raised $500 million in a Series D funding round, valuing the company at nearly $7 billion. The funding follows the company surpassing $1 billion in contract value milestones.

title: Hispasat Obtains WTA Certification for Madrid Teleport
summary: Hispasat's Arganda del Rey Teleport in Madrid has received Tier 4 Full certification from the World Teleport Association (WTA), marking the 80th such certification issued. The achievement highlights Hispasat's commitment to high-quality teleport operations.

title: Planet Labs Wins One-Year Agricultural Data Contract with the Scottish Government
summary: The Scottish Government awarded a one-year, seven-figure contract to Planet Labs for agricultural data via its Computacenter reseller. The deal involves Planet's German subsidiary based in Berlin.

title: Fortastra and Hadrian Sign National Security Spacecraft Manufacturing MoU
summary: Fortastra and Hadrian signed an MoU to collaborate on manufacturing advanced spacecraft for national security missions. The agreement aims to address urgent space-based defense needs through technical partnership.

title: Sophia Space and Caltech File Orbital Data Centers Patent
summary: Sophia Space and Caltech have been issued a patent for space-based data centers, covering architectures for large-scale, modular implementations. The patent, filed in October 2024 and issued in July 2026, highlights advancements in orbital data center technology.

title: SES Optimistic for Second Half Year Bounce after “Soft” Q2
summary: SES reported over 1 billion euros in revenue for the first half of 2026, despite a 'soft' Q2. The company remains optimistic about a rebound in the second half of the year.

title: Starlink’s Link Budget Comes up Short for the D2D Opportunity
summary: SpaceX's Starlink faces technical challenges in its link budget for direct-to-device (D2D) services, despite a large potential market. The analysis highlights concerns about the feasibility of Starlink Mobile's offerings.

title: Cyber Firm Resecurity Joins Space ISAC
summary: Cybersecurity firm Resecurity has joined the Space Information Sharing and Analysis Center (Space ISAC) as a member. The company aims to contribute advanced cyber threat intelligence and digital risk protection capabilities to the space industry.

title: Katalyst Space Encounters Attitude Control Issues With Link Spacecraft
summary: Katalyst Space reported attitude control issues with its recently launched LINK spacecraft, which is part of a mission to rescue NASA’s Swift Observatory. The company provided an update on the technical problems on Tuesday.
